desk.headline: HEPS up 14% to 1 051.9c as hotels and gaming offset weaker media and coal; revenue down 4% to R6.8bn; interim dividend up 17% to 70c; no outlook given
results: HEPS rose 14% to 1 051.9c and headline earnings 10% to R819.8m, even though revenue slipped 4% to R6.8bn and EBITDA fell 9% to R2.41bn.
Hotels led the gains, with headline earnings up 42% to R190.8m; gaming rose 6% to R413.1m and transport and property each added 4%.
Media and broadcasting earnings almost halved (-47% to R55.9m) and coal mining fell 30% to R72.1m; branded products were broadly flat.
The oil and gas prospecting loss widened to R26.5m from R22.2m, while lower losses at head office and other units helped the total.
Net asset value per share grew 8% to R322.90 and the interim dividend was raised 17% to 70c (record date 18 Dec, paid 21 Dec).

guidance.summary: The results announcement gives no earnings outlook or targets for the rest of the year.

watch: Whether hotel and gaming strength holds as Tsogo Sun reported tough October and November trading.
Recovery, or not, in media and coal mining earnings.
The management handover: TG Govender became joint CEO from 1 Sep 2026 and JA Copelyn plans to retire during FY2028; and the oil and gas restructuring through Impact.
